checkResults.scenario: Create an awarding proposal with no event_group_uuid
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2 (Insufficient parameters) from the event_group.blank? guard in Api::ProposalController#create. No proposals row inserted.

2. POST /proposal with an empty body
3. Confirm no proposals row was created
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer with create_proposal rights

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Create an event group with the minimum boundary quantity of 1
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. get_details_for_event_group_line_items sets is_rate_only=false because quantity[:value].to_f is non-zero; EventGroupLineItem is created with meta_data.quantity.value = 1.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a single line item of quantity value 1 and unitSymbol Nos.
2. Assert HTTP 200 and one line item id in the response.
3. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items and assert the stored quantity is 1 and is_rate_only is false.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser; {{productUuid}} and {{productQualityUuid}} are active in the workspace.

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Zero quantity line item is accepted and marked rate-only
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 with is_rate_only true on the stored line item: get_details_for_event_group_line_items sets is_rate_only = true whenever quantity[:value].to_f.zero?. The line item is persisted, not refused.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a single line item of quantity value 0.
2. Assert HTTP 200.
3. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items and assert the item is flagged rate-only rather than rejected.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser; workspace does not require BOQ; {{productUuid}} is active.

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Reject event group creation when line_items is entirely absent
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2 ('Insufficient parameters'), rendered by Api::EventGroupsController#create before authorize EventGroup, because boq_based_rfx is falsy and params[:line_items] is blank. Zero rows written to event_groups.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with status and title only, omitting line_items.
2. Assert HTTP 422 with a numeric error code.
3. Assert no EventGroup row was created for this title.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser; the workspace does NOT have boq_in_erfx_allowed enabled and no config.boq_based_rfx is sent.

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Non-existent product_uuid on line item must not crash event group creation
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 4xx expected (422 with a numeric code). Risk being probed: get_details_for_event_group_line_items does products.find { ... } then dereferences product.id, so an unmatched product would raise NoMethodError on nil and surface as 500. Either way the transaction must roll back and leave zero event_groups rows.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a line item whose product_uuid decodes to an id with no matching active Product.
2. Assert the response is a controlled 4xx and NOT a 500.
3. Assert no partially-created EventGroup is left behind, since create_line_items runs inside the ActiveRecord::Base.transaction.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser. The decoded product id does not exist, or exists but is not Product.active in this workspace.
checkResults.verdict: server error 500 — a 5xx is always a defect

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Negative and non-numeric quantities must not be silently coerced into a valid event
checkResults.expectedResult: No 5xx. Documented hazard: the helper uses quantity[:value].to_f, so 'ten'.to_f becomes 0.0 and silently flips is_rate_only to true, while -5 survives as -5.0. A negative or silently rate-only line item must be refused with a numeric error code rather than persisted.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with two line items: one with quantity value -5 and one with quantity value 'ten'.
2. Assert the response is a controlled 4xx, or if accepted, assert the stored quantities are never negative.
3. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items and inspect the persisted quantity values.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser; {{productUuid}} and {{productQualityUuid}} are active.

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Cross-tenant product_uuid must not be attachable to an event group
checkResults.expectedResult: No 5xx and no data leak. Expected outcome is HTTP 422 with a numeric error code; the created EventGroup (if any) must carry company_id = Current.workspace.id only and must not expose the foreign product's name or quality params in meta_data.
steps: 1. Obtain a product uuid owned by a different tenant.
2. POST /event_groups as company A referencing that foreign {{productUuid}}.
3. Assert the request is refused or the product is not attached, and no cross-tenant product name leaks in the response body.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated as a purchaser of company A. {{productUuid}} is a Product that belongs to company B and is not visible to company A.

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Create draft event group as the seed for an RFP-only project
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. EventGroups::CreateService persists one EventGroup row with status=draft (enum 2) and one EventGroupLineItem with status=draft, serial_number=1 and meta_data.quantity={value:10,unitSymbol:'Nos'}; response is EventGroup::ShowSerializer.
steps: 1. Authenticate as a purchaser of the workspace that owns {{productUuid}}.
2. POST /event_groups with status draft, a title and exactly one line item.
3. Assert HTTP 200 and that the response carries an event_group uuid plus one event_group_line_item id.
4. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} and confirm status is draft with no trade_requests yet.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser with EventGroupPolicy#create? allowed in the workspace; {{productUuid}} and {{productQualityUuid}} resolve to an active Product / ProductQuality in the caller's company.

checkResults.scenario: QA_Platform_Reject RFP stage creation when event_group_uuid is blank
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 888 ('Invalid Parameters') from check_if_allowed_to_add_trade_to_event_group, which returns 888 when EventGroup.find_by(id:, company_id:) is blank. No TradeRequest is persisted.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with an empty event_group_uuid and rfx_mode rfp.
2. Assert HTTP 422 and a numeric error code in the body.
3. Assert no orphan TradeRequest row is created with a null event_group_id.
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated purchaser; no event group is referenced in the payload.
checkResults.verdict: rejected, but for a DIFFERENT reason — this check did not exercise what it claims. Expected "Invalid Parameters", got "Order not active". Usually means a precondition (config or data) isn't met on this client, not a product bug.

2. POST /product_categories with name QA_Platform_Cat_{{stamp}} and hierarchy_type category

checkResults.scenario: Reject category create when name key is absent

checkResults.scenario: Reject category create when hierarchy_type is missing
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. No row created; hierarchy_type is guarded only at the controller level, so this guard is the only thing preventing a NULL hierarchy_type row.

2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 2

checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission

checkResults.scenario: Invalid hierarchy_type enum value must not 500
checkResults.expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. build_product_category calls ProductCategory.new(hierarchy_type: 'supercategory') and the enum {category:0, family:1, commodity:2} raises ArgumentError with no rescue_from in ApplicationController, so an unhandled 500 is the likely real behaviour and is a defect. Acceptable outcome is 422 with a JSON error body.
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with hierarchy_type set to supercategory
2. Assert the HTTP status is below 500
3. Assert the response body is JSON, not an HTML error page
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
checkResults.verdict: server error 500 — a 5xx is always a defect

checkResults.scenario: Wrong-case hierarchy_type CATEGORY must not 500
checkResults.expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. Rails enums are case-sensitive, so 'CATEGORY' is not a member of {category, family, commodity} and hits the same ArgumentError path. Expected safe behaviour is 422 with a JSON error.
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with hierarchy_type set to uppercase CATEGORY
2. Assert status below 500 and a JSON body
3. Assert no row with a NULL hierarchy_type was created
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
checkResults.verdict: server error 500 — a 5xx is always a defect

checkResults.scenario: Reject category create when gst is outside 0-100
checkResults.expectMessage: GST must be a value between 0 and 100
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 865 and message 'GST must be a value between 0 and 100', raised by invalid_gst? before any record is built. No DB write.
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with gst 150.5
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 865
3. Repeat with gst -1 and expect the identical code
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
checkResults.message: GST must be a value between 0 and 100

checkResults.scenario: SQL injection payload in category name must not execute
checkResults.expectedResult: Must not return 5xx and must not execute SQL. ActiveRecord binds the insert, so the payload is stored as a literal string. product_categories must still exist and subsequent reads must succeed.
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with a name containing a DROP TABLE payload
2. Assert status below 500 and a JSON body
3. Re-query GET /product_categories and confirm the table still responds and prior categories are intact
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission; note existing category count

checkResults.scenario: XSS payload in category name is stripped by param sanitizer
checkResults.expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. ParamsAuth#sanitize_input_params runs strip_html_tags_except_mentions on every string param before the action, so the persisted and echoed name must have the script tags removed.
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with a script tag embedded in the name
2. Assert status below 500
3. Read the returned name and assert it contains no script markup
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
checkResults.verdict: handled safely — refused cleanly (HTTP 403), no crash

checkResults.scenario: Reject product create when category_uuid is absent

checkResults.scenario: Reject duplicate product_code within the same company
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 8 and the product_code taken_already message from Product#duplicate_product_code. The conflict scope is Product.where(status: [:active, :draft, :in_review, :rejected]), so an in_active twin would NOT trigger it.

2. POST /products again with the same product_code and a different name
3. Assert HTTP 422 and that only one product carries that code

checkResults.message: The Article Code QA_Platform_DupCode is already taken!

checkResults.scenario: Invalid product_type enum must not 500
checkResults.expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. Products::CreateService assigns product.product_type directly; an unknown enum member raises ArgumentError. The action only rescues ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, so a 500 is the likely real outcome and is a defect.
steps: 1. POST /products with product_type set to a value outside the enum
2. Assert the status is below 500 and the body is JSON
3. Assert no product row was created with a NULL product_type
checkResults.preconditions: Family uuid bound to {{familyUuid}}; user has product create_record permission

checkResults.scenario: XSS payload in product name and variant name is sanitized
checkResults.expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. sanitize_object recurses through nested hashes and arrays, so both the top-level name and variants[0].name are passed through strip_html_tags_except_mentions before the controller runs.
steps: 1. POST /products with an img onerror payload in name and a script tag in the variant name
2. Assert status below 500
3. Assert neither the response nor the stored product_qualities row contains executable markup
checkResults.preconditions: Family uuid bound to {{familyUuid}}; user has product create_record permission
checkResults.verdict: handled safely — refused cleanly (HTTP 403), no crash

checkResults.scenario: SQL injection payload in product_code must not execute
checkResults.expectedResult: Must not return 5xx and must not leak DB metadata. The value is stored as a literal string via a bound insert. Critically, Product.autocomplete_search interpolates the query into a raw where clause, so the stored value must also be safe to read back.
steps: 1. POST /products with a UNION SELECT payload as the product_code
2. Assert the status is below 500
3. Call GET /products/search with a harmless query and confirm the products table still responds normally
checkResults.preconditions: Family uuid bound to {{familyUuid}}; note the current product count
checkResults.message: The Article Code QA_Platform_' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL,version()-- is already taken!
checkResults.verdict: handled safely — refused cleanly (HTTP 422), no crash

checkResults.scenario: PR list page 1 returns the documented envelope
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 from PurchaseRequests::ViewService. Default page size is 50. closure_configuration mirrors CustomConfiguration is_pr_partial_closure_enabled. No DB writes.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with page=1 and a status filter
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert keys purchase_requests, total_pages, total_pr_count, columns_configuration, closure_configuration
4. Assert each purchase_request carries rfq_no and a line_items array with the four quantity fields
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has at least one PurchaseRequest not in status in_active with line items.

checkResults.scenario: PR list page=0 collapses to page 1
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. PurchaseRequests::SearchQuery sets @page = [1, params[:page].to_i].max, so 0, negative and non-numeric all resolve to page 1.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 and record the PR uuid list
2. GET /purchase_requests?page=0
3. Assert both return the same first-page payload
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has more than 50 PR line items so page 1 and page 2 differ.

checkResults.scenario: PR list far-out page returns an empty page with a real total_pages
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200, empty purchase_requests. Kaminari yields an empty relation; total_pages must remain the true page count.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=999999 with a status filter
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert purchase_requests is empty
4. Assert total_pages and total_pr_count still describe the full result set
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has fewer than 999999 pages of PR items.

checkResults.scenario: ageing_status=breach returns only items aged at or beyond the breach threshold
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. filter_by_ageing_status applies AGEING_DAYS_EXPR >= AGEING_BREACH_THRESHOLD (7). 'warning' is the 4..6 band.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with ageing_status breach
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert every returned line item reports ageing_in_days >= 7
4. Assert items younger than 4 days are absent
checkResults.preconditions: Config purchase_request_ageing_enabled is ON. Workspace has PR items older than 7 days with no PO, plus items younger than 4 days.

checkResults.scenario: Unrecognised ageing_status value is ignored instead of erroring
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. The case/else branch logs 'Unrecognized filter' and adds no condition, so the original relation is returned unfiltered.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with an unknown ageing_status value
2. Assert HTTP 200 and a result set equal to the unfiltered active list
checkResults.preconditions: Config purchase_request_ageing_enabled is ON.

checkResults.scenario: is_dormant filter returns only PRs past the dormant threshold and not yet unlocked
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. The scope dormant_locked_for_company requires status active, dormant_unlocked_at IS NULL and CURRENT_DATE - created_at::date >= threshold.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with is_dormant true
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert the old locked PR is present
4. Assert the newer PR and the already-unlocked PR are absent
checkResults.preconditions: Config pr_dormant_threshold_days has a value > 0. Workspace has a PR older than the threshold with dormant_unlocked_at NULL, one newer PR, and one already unlocked.

checkResults.scenario: is_dormant filter is a no-op when the dormant feature is not configured
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 identical to the unfiltered call. filter_by_dormant_status returns the untouched relation when dormant_feature_enabled_for? is false, so the scope - whose SQL would bind a nil threshold - is never built.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with only a status filter and record the PR ids
2. GET the same URL with is_dormant true added
3. Assert both responses are HTTP 200 with identical PR id sets
checkResults.preconditions: CustomConfiguration pr_dormant_threshold_days is absent, or its value is 0.

checkResults.scenario: PR list cannot be steered to another company's PRs via pr_ids
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 with an empty result. The base relation is scoped for_companies([Current.workspace.id]) and the pr_ids scope only narrows it further - it can never widen it.
steps: 1. As a workspace-A user, GET /purchase_requests filtered by a PR id from workspace B
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert purchase_requests is empty and total_pr_count is 0
4. Assert no rfq_no or line item from that PR appears
checkResults.preconditions: Two workspaces A and B. A PR belongs to workspace B. Authenticate as a workspace-A user.

checkResults.scenario: Injection payload in the rfq_no filter is escaped by sql_like
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200, no rows matched by the tautology. The scopes route the value through PurchaseRequest.sql_like before the ILIKE bind, so both the quote and the wildcard are neutralised.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with an injection payload in the rfq_no filter
2. Assert HTTP 200 and an empty or normally-filtered result
3. Assert the purchase_requests table is intact
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer user with at least one PR in the workspace.

checkResults.scenario: Malformed filters JSON does not produce a 5xx
checkResults.expectedResult: No 500. create_filter_params delegates to CommonFunctions.parse_filters; a truncated JSON string must not escape as an unrescued JSON::ParserError to the client.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests with a truncated filters JSON string
2. Assert the response is not a 5xx
3. Assert either a normal 200 envelope or a deterministic 4xx
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer user.
checkResults.verdict: server error 500 — a 5xx is always a defect

checkResults.verdict: server error 500 — a 5xx is always a defect

checkResults.scenario: Wrong-case role SUPER_ADMIN must not 500
checkResults.expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. The 757 guard compares args['role'] == 'super_admin' with an exact string match, so 'SUPER_ADMIN' bypasses that check entirely and falls through to the case-sensitive enum assignment, raising ArgumentError.
steps: 1. POST /users/create_user with role in upper case
2. Assert status below 500 and JSON body
3. Assert no user with a NULL role was created
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated admin with user create_record permission; unused phone and email
checkResults.verdict: server error 500 — a 5xx is always a defect

checkResults.scenario: all_vendors returns paginated vendor list with onboarding counters
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 rendering api/companies/all_companies. Companies ordered by name ASC. All four onboarding counters present and >= 0. No DB writes.
steps: 1. Authenticate as a buyer user of the workspace
2. GET /companies/all_vendors?page=1
3. Assert HTTP 200
4. Assert body carries total_pages, total_vendors, active_vendors, total_verified_vendors, total_unverified_vendors, total_in_progress_vendors, total_rejected_vendors
5. Assert every returned company id has a vendor_mapping_data entry
checkResults.preconditions: Buyer workspace has at least one BuyerSellerCompanyMapping in status active/invited/blacklisted; vendor Company is active. User has Company policy read access.

checkResults.scenario: all_vendors page=0 is coerced to page 1
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. Api::CompaniesController#paginate sets @page_number = 1 and only overrides when params['page'].to_i > 0, so page=0 returns exactly the page-1 result set.
steps: 1. GET /companies/all_vendors?page=1 and record the company id list
2. GET /companies/all_vendors?page=0
3. Compare the id lists
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has more vendors than one page.

checkResults.scenario: all_vendors far-out page number returns an empty page, not a 500
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 with an empty companies array. total_vendors/total_pages remain the real values. companies.total_pages must not raise.
steps: 1. GET /companies/all_vendors?page=999999
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert companies list is empty and total_pages still reflects the real page count
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has fewer than 999999 pages of vendors.

checkResults.scenario: all_vendors Excel export with zero matching vendors is refused with code 494
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 494 'No Vendors found.' download_vendors_sheet and get_signed_url are never invoked; no S3 object is written.
steps: 1. GET /companies/all_vendors with download_excel=true and a filter matching nothing
2. Assert the request is rejected before any report generation
3. Assert no report_url is returned
checkResults.preconditions: Apply a filter set that matches no vendor for this workspace.
checkResults.verdict: ACCEPTED input that should have been rejected (HTTP 200)

checkResults.scenario: vendorlist_filtered without query param is rejected with code 2
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (render_error_json(2) fires on `unless query_string`). No companies/tags keys in the body.
steps: 1. GET /companies/vendorlist_filtered with no query parameter
2. Assert rejection before any DB search runs
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer user with Company policy read access.

checkResults.scenario: vendorlist_filtered matches name/email/vendor_code and paginates at 10 per page
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200. The ILIKE runs over companies.name, companies.email and buyer_seller_company_mappings.vendor_code as a single bound :query. Page size is fixed at 10. total_pages is never 0.
steps: 1. GET /companies/vendorlist_filtered with a query and page=1
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert companies, tags, total_count and total_pages are present
4. Assert companies length <= 10
checkResults.preconditions: Workspace has a vendor whose company name, email or BSM vendor_code contains a known substring.

checkResults.scenario: vendorlist_filtered SQL-injection payload is bound, not interpolated
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200, zero or normal matches. The query reaches Postgres as the bound parameter in an ILIKE; no rows are returned by a tautology and no statement error is raised.
steps: 1. GET /companies/vendorlist_filtered with query set to a SQL-injection payload
2. Assert HTTP 200 with an empty companies list
3. Assert buyer_seller_company_mappings and companies tables are intact afterwards
checkResults.preconditions: Authenticated buyer user.

checkResults.scenario: vendorlist_filtered never returns another buyer's vendor mappings
checkResults.expectedResult: HTTP 200 with vendor V absent. The base relation filters client_company_id: Current.workspace.id, so vendor V cannot surface.
steps: 1. As a workspace-A user, GET /companies/vendorlist_filtered with vendor V's name
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert vendor V is absent from companies and from every tag's taggable_companies
checkResults.preconditions: Two buyer workspaces A and B. Vendor V is mapped to workspace B only. Authenticate as a user of workspace A.
